doc.title: Emile Christian and Anthony Sbarbaro Interview, 1959-02-11

title: Vega and trumpet styles today
summary: Sbarbaro judges Vega and modern high-note trumpet playing.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Vega was a good trumpet player, any way you're looking. That's a hard thing for a man like Butterfield. A fellow will say, that man can play anywhere. What could Vega do? Vega could play trumpet.
That's the answer. You want to know if he could read to perfection, that's a that's a horse of a different color. But he was a good trumpet player.

Just like whoever's down here now, you see Al Hurth, I need to mention that, but he's a good trumpet player. What particular style you don't like about him, that's, you know, you can pick on most any man.
Well, I mean, did he have a good ratty tone, a good beat, all that?
How many trumpet players in New Orleans in those days could hit the high notes the fellows are hitting today?
I don't know. I don't even care.
You know? That's what I mean. That's a... You see, today's a different school.
God, we get some of these fellows that can go and they never stop. They don't know what stop means. Can they play hot? Yes, but their style. Yeah. Depends if you like his style, if he plays, but...
See what they like, see how many high notes they can hit. I don't like a lot of their styles and I can't do nothing about it. It wasn't, it wasn't the high notes. I cannot go and listen to them.
that's what I do. Swinging that punch in there. That was it. There he is. Look at him.
